real-estate-agent.definition: A licensed or authorized professional who helps clients buy, sell, or rent property.
real-estate-agent.exampleUsage: The real-estate agent arranged a property viewing.

broker.definition: A person who helps clients buy, sell, or rent property.

appraiser.definition: A person who estimates officially the worth or value or quality of things.

mortgage-lender.definition: A bank, company, or other institution that provides loans secured by real property under agreed terms.
mortgage-lender.exampleUsage: The mortgage lender reviewed the adult applicant's documents.

title-agent.definition: A professional who researches property ownership records and helps manage title or closing documents in some property transactions.
title-agent.exampleUsage: The title agent checked the property records.

property-manager.definition: A person or company responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, or rental administration of property.
property-manager.exampleUsage: The property manager arranged a repair for the building.

developer.definition: A person who develops real estate (especially someone who prepares a site for residential or commercial use).

contractor.definition: Someone (a person or firm) who contracts to build things.

architect.definition: A person who designs buildings and prepares their plans.

listing.definition: A database containing an ordered array of items (names or topics).

open-house.definition: A planned public event allows visitors to enter a property, institution, or venue, inspect it, and ask questions without making separate appointments.

showing.definition: The display of a motion picture.

counter-offer.definition: A new offer made in response to an earlier offer, changing one or more proposed terms.
counter-offer.exampleUsage: The seller responded to the original price with a counter-offer.

negotiation.definition: A discussion intended to produce an agreement.

appraisal.definition: A document appraising the value of something (as for insurance or taxation).

escrow.definition: A written agreement (or property or money) delivered to a third party or put in trust by one party to a contract to be returned after fulfillment of some condition.

mortgage.definition: A conditional conveyance of property as security for the repayment of a loan.

down-payment.definition: Part of a purchase price paid at the start, with the remaining amount paid or borrowed over time.

interest-rate.definition: A percentage showing what borrowing money costs or what saving and lending it can earn over a set period, usually one year.

closing-costs.definition: Fees and expenses connected with completing a real-estate purchase or mortgage, separate from the property's price.
closing-costs.exampleUsage: The buyer's worksheet lists estimated closing costs.

equity.definition: The difference between the market value of a property and the claims held against it.

appreciation.definition: An increase in price or value.

depreciation.definition: A decrease in price or value.

tax-assessment.definition: An official valuation or calculation used by a government authority to determine property tax or another tax obligation.
tax-assessment.exampleUsage: The property record includes the latest tax assessment.

hoa-fee.definition: A regular fee paid by members of a homeowners association for shared services, maintenance, or community expenses.
hoa-fee.exampleUsage: The listing states the monthly HOA fee.

pre-approval.definition: A preliminary decision from a lender indicating how much an eligible borrower may be able to borrow, subject to later checks and conditions.
pre-approval.exampleUsage: The adult buyer received mortgage pre-approval before making an offer.

listing-agreement.definition: A contract between a property owner and a real-estate professional setting the terms for marketing and selling or renting the property.
listing-agreement.exampleUsage: The owner reviewed the listing agreement before signing.

purchase-agreement.definition: A legally enforceable contract sets out what one party will purchase and what another will provide, along with the agreed terms.

deed.definition: A legal document signed and sealed and delivered to effect a transfer of property and to show the legal right to possess it.

title.definition: A legal document signed and sealed and delivered to effect a transfer of property and to show the legal right to possess it.

mortgage-note.definition: A legal document in which a borrower promises to repay a mortgage loan according to stated terms.
mortgage-note.exampleUsage: The closing file contains a signed mortgage note.

disclosure.definition: The speech act of making something evident.

insurance-policy.definition: A contract describing the coverage, conditions, limits, and responsibilities of an insurance agreement.
insurance-policy.exampleUsage: The homeowner reviewed the insurance policy details.

tax-return.definition: A document submitted to tax authorities that reports how much tax a person owes.

proof-of-income.definition: Documents or records used to show how much income a person receives.
proof-of-income.exampleUsage: The lender requested proof of income from the adult applicant.
